title: Operator investigation decision tree and panel triage
content:
Purpose: Short, operator-focused playbook to speed up incident investigation for inference regressions (latency, error, cost). This doc is intentionally compact and workflow-driven so oncall and SRE can follow a decision tree, identify the minimal panels needed, and collect traces with cost-sensitive sampling.

Quick TL;DR:
- When an alert fires, follow the decision tree below to narrow root cause quickly.
- Start with 3 panels (latency heat, request deck, failure taxonomy) then expand based on first answer branch.
- Use targeted trace anchors (model id, route, backend host) and adaptive sampling to keep trace volume bounded.
- Post-incident: add one concrete metric or dashboard panel that would have shortened the investigation.

Scope & assumptions:
- Covers token-serving, multi-model routing, and cache (KV/prefix) behaviors only; not infra host-level or networking-only incidents.
- Multi-tenant signals are expected; the decision tree highlights tenant-weighted attribution where needed.
- This is a compact operational tool; canonical metric definitions live in metric-contracts repo.

Decision tree (operator-first):
1) What triggered the alert?
   - High P50/P95 token-latency -> go to path A.
   - Elevated 5xx or model errors -> go to path B.
   - Sudden spike in cost/token spend (unexpected billable tokens) -> go to path C.
   - Broad customer impact with mixed symptoms -> start full triage (A+B+C) and escalate.

Path A (latency):
- Step A1: Is latency localized to a single model or route? Check panel: per-model P50/P95 for last 15m (panel 1). If single model -> A2. If widespread -> A4.
- Step A2: Check KV cache hit rate and prefix-warmth for that model + tenant. Low hit => cold-cache path. Panels: cache hit heatmap, tenant cold-start index.
- Step A3: If cache warm and still high latency -> check GPU host metrics (core utilization, mem pressure) and batching queue depth. If GPU saturation -> signal capacity autoscale or Dedicated pool fallback.
- Step A4: Widespread latency -> check routing policy failovers, recent rollout IDs, canary flags. Pull the rollout widget and trace for a canary session.

Path B (errors):
- Step B1: Classify errors by type: model error (nan, oom), runtime error (kernel crash), infra (transport/connect). Use failure taxonomy panel that groups errors by error_code and model_version.
- Step B2: If OOM/model-failure: capture trace with kv-cache=false (to remove caching layer) and include model variant, quantization layer. Escalate to applied-ml if classifier model exhibits accuracy/regression alarms.
- Step B3: If transport/connect: check recent node restarts and control-plane traces (route decision logs).

Path C (cost spike):
- Step C1: Is spike due to token volume or per-token cost change? Use token-rate panel and per-token-cost-timeseries.
- Step C2: If token-rate spike: check upstream event (customer spam, batch job). Use tenant request deck (sampled prompts + prompt-size histogram). Block offending key if malicious.
- Step C3: If per-token cost increase: check fallback routing (fell back to larger model) and quantization profile shifts. Re-route to cheaper variant if safe.

Minimal panels to launch on alert (operator starter kit):
- Panel A: Per-model latency (P50/P90/P95) by model_version, last 1h/15m.
- Panel B: Request deck (sampled prompts, tenant, size, route).
- Panel C: Failure taxonomy (group by error_type, model_version).
- Panel D: Cache warmth & KV hit rate by tenant/model.
- Panel E: Routing & rollout events (recent deploys, canary flags).
- Panel F: Token volume & per-token cost trend.
Panel composition note: Keep each panel filtered by time-range dropdown; default to 15m for incidents.

Candidate SLI/SLOs (compact and operator-oriented):
- SLI: served_token_latency_p95 (model_route) -> description: 95th token generation latency observed at response boundary.
- Alert threshold candidate: p95 > 500ms for > 5min for hosted API tier.
- SLI: model_inference_error_rate (5xx per 1k requests) -> alert when > 10 errors/1k sustained for 10m.
- SLI: kv_cache_hit_rate (tenant_model) -> target > 85% for warm workloads; alert if < 40% and latency elevated.
- SLI: routing_fallback_rate -> percent of requests routed to larger model variant due to capacity/compatibility fallback; alert if > 2% sustained for > 10m without explicit rollout.

Trace anchors & sampling guidance: (cost-aware)
- Anchor traces on: request_id, model_id, selected_kernel, backend_host, tenant_id. That gives minimal context for reconstructing path.
- Sampling policy: default 0.5% global sampling for traces. On alert set adaptive sampling:
   - If alert is per-tenant: sample 100% of traces for that tenant for 15m.
   - If alert is per-model: sample 5% for that model, 0.5% otherwise.
   - For errors (5xx/oom): always sample 100% until error rate drops below threshold.
- Keep trace payload redaction rules: remove PII from prompts and store prompt-hash + truncated prompt (first 80 chars) only. Use prompt-hash to join with request deck in dashboards.

Panel prioritization matrix (how to expand beyond starter kit):
- Triage impact vs cost axis:
   - High impact, low cost: per-model P95 latency, failure taxonomy, request deck -> build first.
   - High impact, high cost: full trace replay, session reconstruction -> enable for long-lived incidents only.
   - Low impact, low cost: tenant cold-start index, kv-cache histograms -> schedule next sprint.
   - Low impact, high cost: full prompt replays for sample sets -> avoid unless requested by product/CS.

Runbook snippets (copyable):
- To collect a focused trace: set sampling filter: tenant_id=<id> OR model_id=<id>; include kv_cache=false tag; capture 120s pre-alert, 60s post-alert. Upload trace link to incident ticket.
- To block suspected mass-requester: find top 10 tenant request rates in request deck, identify API key, run kill-key script (ops-runbook: API-KEY-BLOCK).

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- How strongly should we tie alerting thresholds to model size? (p50/p95 baselines differ a lot by model family). Proposal: per-model baselines with tiered thresholds; need product input on SLA tiers.
- Cost cap for trace retention on high-volume tenants — current budget unclear. Suggest per-tenant daily trace quota to prevent runaway cost.
- Do we allow sampling policies to be modified by non-SRE (e.g., oncall PMs)? We need guardrails.

Action items & owners:
- Marisol: prototype templated incident dashboard that auto-populates the starter kit panels (target: 2025-03-09).
- Leo: add routing_fallback_rate metric to metric-contracts and emit in runtime (JIRA-OBS-7489) (target: 2025-03-05).
- Rina: draft trace-quota proposal and cost estimate for tenant-level retention (target: 2025-03-12).
- Marcus: create pattern-matching snapshot for OOM errors to include quantization and kernel selection in traces (target: 2025-03-02).

Post-incident checklist (for postmortem):
- Did we have the minimal 3 panels up in the first 10m? If no, add panel to dashboard template.
- Did traces provide the necessary anchors (model_id, tenant_id, request_id)? If not, add missing trace tags.
- Identify one measurable metric/panel to add to reduce future time-to-detect or time-to-resolve.

Notes to self: keep this doc short; link to canonical metric-contracts and long-form playbooks. This is meant to be a quick operator cheat-sheet and triage decision tree rather than a canonical spec.

References: Confluence investigation playbooks, metric-contracts repo, and PRs listed above.

Feedback requested: anyone on observability team — does the starter kit panels cover 80% of oncall investigations? If not, what single panel would save most time?
